Folks — quick triage notes after initial checks:
- Scope: Elevated 5xx + latent tokenization stalls originating from inference hosts in us-west-2a. Error traces show repeated kernel fallbacks on a subset of quantized model instances; CPU thrashing observed on host nodes (likely noisy-neighbor / NIC transmit queue backpressure).
- Impact: VertexHealth ~22% of their production traffic on AZ1 is timing out; overall customer p95 up ~3x.
- Short-term mitigation (now): 1) Immediate partial traffic diversion (20-40%) for Vertex to us-west-2b where compatible model variants are warm, 2) Disable live-quantization path for a small slice of instances to reduce kernel fallback storms (temp config), 3) Increase request timeouts and activate KV-prefix cache for Vertex route.
- Longer-term: replace noisy hosts (SRE), evaluate autoscale thresholds for quantized pools, and update our kernel selection policy to avoid fallback loops.

Marcus — can you confirm we have capacity in us-west-2b and that the model variant mapping is compatible for a targeted partial diversion? If yes, I recommend we execute the 20–40% diversion now and monitor 15m.

Hannah / Vanessa — this will require an authorization decision for an emergency cross-region steer beyond standard control plane (it’s an SLA-impacting mitigation). I also recommend pre-approving an operational credit if diversion causes higher token/unit usage.

Soojin
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency spike + 5xx surge (AZ1) — please triage + exec eyes

Confirming capacity check: us-west-2b has warm instances for Vertex’s model family (redwood/gpt-large-q4 variant). We can accept a partial diversion of 30% immediately. Plan:
1) At 09:35 PT rotate LB weight for Vertex route: AZ1 -> AZ1:70%, AZ2(2b) -> 30%.
2) Toggle quantization fallback guardrails for the targeted instances (config id: qguard-2027-04-07) to force the safer kernel path.
3) Monitor 5xx rate and p95 for 20-minute windows; if error rate drops <1% and p95 reduces we can step up to 60% diversion.

Operational notes: will need a short DocuSign approval line from Vertex (change-of-routing consent) for cross-region traffic steering per our contract (I’ll paste the template). Rafael — can you ping Andrew for a quick e-sign? Vanessa — please prepare comms (customer play advisory + internal exec note) and flag if billing/credit is needed.

— Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
